new_articles.title: Kia plans India plant expansion as sales surge; aims 410,000 units by 2030
new_articles.summary: Kia 관련 기사다. 기사 제목은 'Kia plans India plant expansion as sales surge; aims 410,000 units by 2030'이다. Kia India plans to expand its manufacturing capacity to meet future demand. The automaker targets annual sales of 410,000 vehicles by the year 2030. Kia will introduce ten new vehicles, with eight being electrified models. The company is also expanding its network into smaller Indian cities. This expansion aims to serve both domestic customers and increase exports. Reuters Kia plans to expand India capacity as sales growth accelerates New Delhi: South Korea’s Kia Corp plans to expand its car manufacturing capacity in India to meet expected growth in domestic sales and overseas demand The automaker, which clocked 17% sales volume growth to 191,949 vehicles in the first seven months of 2026, is targeting annual sales of 410,000 vehicles by 2030, Atul Sood, senior vice-president, marketing and sales at Kia India, told ET ” India is the fourth-largest market for Kia, accounting for 10% of its global sales Also Read: Kia India to raise vehicle prices by up to 2% from July 1 Data from the road ministry’s Vahan portal showed that electric car sales in India surged 90% year-on-year during March-July 2026 Kia is also working on widening its pan-India network by entering more Tier 3 and Tier 4 cities.

matched_articles.title: Why does SK Hynix want to sell its chip facility in southwest China?
matched_articles.summary: SK hynix 관련 기사다. 기사 제목은 'Why does SK Hynix want to sell its chip facility in southwest China?'이다. South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix’s potential deal to offload a packaging plant in southwest China is part of a strategic pivot towards higher-margin artificial intelligence memory products, according to analysts. But they cautioned a sale might not be straightforward, as the memory chip giant would need to navigate valuation hurdles and a volatile chip cycle. SK Hynix said on Monday it was “looking into various solutions to enhance the competitiveness of its packaging business”, after reports. . The South Korean chipmaker wants to pivot towards the high-margin AI memory sector, but analysts warn any sale would face valuation hurdles 2 -MIN READ 2 -MIN 1 Listen Ann Cao in Shanghai and Howard Liu in Beijing Published: 10:00am, 12 Aug 2026 Updated: 5:08pm, 12 Aug 2026 South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix’s potential deal to offload a packaging plant in southwest China is part of a strategic pivot towards higher-margin artificial intelligence memory products, according to analysts SK Hynix said on Monday it was “looking into various solutions to enhance the competitiveness of its packaging business”, after reports emerged last week it was weighing options for its facility in Chongqing, a megacity in China’s southwest SK Hynix said in a statement that no final decisions had been made The Chongqing plant functions as a back-end hub focused on downstream packaging and testing for SK Hynix’s NAND flash memory products com, described SK Hynix’s decision as a strategic shift from low-value back-end assembly to high-margin front-end manufacturing. 이 기사는 해당 기업과 연결된 해외 보도를 바탕으로 정리했다.
